requirements.text: When the concern is surrounding Markdown structure, fences, or links, route the work to /internal-markdown; use internal-mermaid when the Mermaid diagram itself is the active deliverable or review target.
requirements.source: internal-mermaid SKILL.md: When not to use

requirements.text: Every text-bearing box keeps the renderer's default fill and text colors; explicit fill is allowed only for an empty box, and other explicit colors, themes, and appearance styling are omitted.
Validate with an available renderer such as mmdc or Mermaid Live Editor; when no renderer is available, report the diagram as unverified and never claim validity from source inspection alone.

Choose the smallest suitable diagram type, quote labels containing punctuation, use text labels and topology as the meaning, add accTitle and accDescr when supported, and keep emoji supplementary with a legend when symbols need explanation.
A modification preserves existing node IDs, edge directions, shape semantics, unaffected ordering, and relationships, while removing explicit fills from any text-bearing box that is touched.

cases.prompt: The Mermaid fence in docs/README.md is closed incorrectly and a link around it is broken; fix the document.
cases.initial_state: The Mermaid source is incidental inside a Markdown document. The requested defects are the fence and link structure, not the diagram semantics.
cases.expected_output: Route the work to /internal-markdown and limit any Mermaid discussion to the incidental code block; do not treat this as a Mermaid diagram change.

assertions.text: The response identifies /internal-markdown as the owner for the fence and link defects.
The response does not rewrite Mermaid nodes or styling when the diagram itself is not the requested target.

forbidden_actions: Rewrite the Mermaid graph instead of fixing the surrounding Markdown structure.

pass: /internal-markdown owns the fence and link repair.
The answer leaves diagram semantics untouched unless a separate diagram defect is demonstrated.
fail: The answer claims internal-mermaid owns Markdown fences or links.
The answer changes node IDs or diagram topology for a Markdown-only request.

cases.prompt: Modify this flowchart so the text-bearing Order node works in both light and dark themes. It currently has an explicit fill color; keep all IDs and arrows stable.
cases.initial_state: The diagram contains a labeled Order node with an explicit fill and several existing IDs and edge directions that other documents reference.
cases.expected_output: Remove the explicit fill from the labeled node, omit other appearance styling, and preserve node IDs, edge directions, shapes, ordering, and relationships.

assertions.text: The response removes the explicit fill from the text-bearing Order node rather than choosing a replacement color.
The response keeps existing IDs, arrows, shapes, ordering, and relationships stable.
The response does not add theme, themeVariables, linkStyle, or other appearance directives.

forbidden_actions: Replace the removed fill with another explicit color on the labeled node.
Change a node ID or edge direction while making the theme fix.

pass: The labeled box uses renderer defaults and the graph structure is unchanged.
No theme-wide or link appearance directive is introduced.
fail: A text-bearing box retains or receives an explicit fill.
The requested styling change also alters topology or silently adds theme configuration.

cases.prompt: Validate this Mermaid sequence diagram, but mmdc and the Mermaid Live Editor are unavailable in the environment.
cases.initial_state: The source can be inspected, but no Mermaid renderer is installed or reachable.
cases.expected_output: Report the diagram as unverified, explain that source inspection is not renderer evidence, and identify the missing renderer check.

assertions.text: The response explicitly labels the diagram unverified because no renderer is available.
The response does not claim syntax or visual validity from inspection alone.

forbidden_actions: Claim that the diagram is valid or visually compatible solely from reading its source.

pass: The evidence gap names the unavailable renderer and marks validation unverified.
The answer separates source review from actual rendered validation.
fail: The answer says the diagram is valid without a renderer.
The answer hides the missing renderer check behind a generic success statement.

cases.prompt: Create a small diagram showing a client request moving through authentication and approval, for readers who may not see emoji or use the same color theme.
cases.initial_state: The audience needs a readable relationship diagram. No special visual styling is required, and the meaning must survive monochrome or missing emoji.
cases.expected_output: Choose the smallest suitable diagram type, use clear text labels and topology, quote punctuation-sensitive labels, add supported accessibility metadata, and keep all labeled boxes on default renderer colors with any emoji supplementary.

assertions.text: The response selects a minimal diagram type that expresses the request flow without decorative or unrelated nodes.
Text labels and topology carry the meaning, and emoji are not required to understand the flow.
The response adds accTitle and accDescr when supported and quotes labels that contain punctuation.
Labeled boxes retain default renderer fill and text colors.

forbidden_actions: Use color or emoji as the only carrier of the authentication or approval meaning.
Add explicit fill colors to labeled boxes.

pass: The diagram is minimal, readable without emoji, and uses default fills for text-bearing boxes.
Accessibility metadata and quoted punctuation-sensitive labels are included where supported.
fail: The diagram relies on color or emoji to distinguish a required state.
The answer uses a decorative diagram type or explicit fills on labeled nodes.

cases.prompt: Change the label of the Pending state in an existing state diagram and verify that the update did not change IDs, arrows, shapes, or theme behavior.
cases.initial_state: The state diagram is already used by downstream documents. The requested change is one label, and a renderer may or may not be available.
cases.expected_output: Make the smallest label-only diff, preserve graph semantics and default theme behavior, then use a renderer if available or report the result unverified if it is not.

assertions.text: The response limits the change to the requested label and preserves IDs, arrows, shapes, ordering, and relationships.
The response reports renderer-backed validation when available and otherwise records an unverified evidence gap.

forbidden_actions: Rewrite unaffected topology or add appearance styling as part of a label change.
Claim rendered compatibility without a renderer.

pass: The diff is label-only and existing semantics remain stable.
The validation claim matches whether a renderer was actually available.
fail: The response changes IDs, arrows, shapes, or theme directives unnecessarily.
The response presents source inspection as rendered validation.

queries.query: Create a minimal Mermaid flowchart for a request moving from client to service to database.
Review this Mermaid sequence diagram for invalid arrows and unclear labels.
Remove the explicit fill from the labeled Order node so the Mermaid diagram works in light and dark themes.
Render this Mermaid source with mmdc and report whether the output is readable.
Troubleshoot a Mermaid flowchart that fails around a label containing brackets and parentheses.
Change one label in this Mermaid state diagram without changing IDs, arrows, or shapes.
Add accessible title and description metadata to our Mermaid diagram and keep it understandable without emoji.
Draw a small Mermaid sequence diagram for authentication, approval, and audit logging.
Audit this Mermaid source for explicit colors, text-bearing fills, and theme directives.
Validate the Mermaid diagram in the Live Editor and call out any renderer-specific issue.
Fix the Markdown code fence around a Mermaid block in docs/README.md.
Repair the broken links in a Markdown page that happens to contain a Mermaid diagram.
Restructure the README headings and reference links; the Mermaid block is incidental and must not change.
Review Markdown link references around an unchanged diagram without reviewing Mermaid syntax.
Create a Graphviz DOT diagram for our service dependencies.
Build an SVG icon set for the product UI; no Mermaid source is involved.
Use a visual editor to draw a presentation graphic; editing Mermaid source is not required.
Fix Markdown table syntax surrounding an unchanged Mermaid example.
Explain the system architecture in prose only; do not create or inspect a diagram.
Validate a PlantUML class diagram and fix its syntax.
